result.topic_en: Euler completes the partial-fraction expansion of $\frac{1}{x^m(x+a)^n}$ and uses it to express the sum of the series $\sum \frac{1}{k^m(a+k)^n}$ in terms of the power sums $\int\frac{1}{z^\lambda}$ (zeta-type sums).
result.transcription:
148 MEDITATIONES CIRCA
$\pm\frac{1}{a^m}\cdot\frac{1}{(x+a)^n}\pm\frac{m}{1.a^{m+1}}\cdot\frac{1}{(x+a)^{n-1}}\pm\frac{m(m+1)}{1.2.a^{m+2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(x+a)^{n-2}}$
$\pm\frac{m(m+1)(m+2)}{1.2.3\,a^{m+3}}\cdot\frac{1}{(x+a)^{n-3}}\pm\text{etc.}$
vbi tenendum eſt, in inferiori ordine ſignum ſuperius $+$ valere, ſi $m$ ſit numerus par, contra vero ſignum inferius; tum vero vterque ordo non vlterius continuari debet, quam vsque ad terminos vbi exponens poteſtatum ipſius $x$ et $x+a$ ad vnitatem fuerit diminutus.
7. Hinc igitur primo ſummam huius ſeriei
$\frac{1}{1(a+1)^n}+\frac{1}{2^m(a+2)^n}+\frac{1}{3^m(a+3)^n}+\frac{1}{4^m(a+4)^n}+\text{etc.}=s$
definire licet, dum in forma modo exhibita loco $x$ omnes numeri 1, 2, 3 etc. in infinitum ſubſtituuntur, et in vnam ſummam colliguntur: Quoniam enim omnes termini ex formula $A.\frac{1}{x^\lambda}$ nati dant ſeriem cuius ſummam per $A\int\frac{1}{z^\lambda}$ exprimimus, ex formula autem $A\frac{1}{(x+a)^\lambda}$ prodit ſeries cuius ſumma eſt $A\int\frac{1}{z^\lambda}-A\left(1+\frac{1}{2^\lambda}+\frac{1}{3^\lambda}\,....+\frac{1}{a^\lambda}\right)$, ſeriei noſtrae ſumma ita ſe habebit:
$s=\frac{1}{a^n}\int\frac{1}{z^m}-\frac{n}{1.a^{n+1}}\int\frac{1}{z^{m-1}}+\frac{n(n+1)}{1.2\,a^{n+2}}\int\frac{1}{z^{m-2}}$
$-\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1.2.3\,a^{n+3}}\int\frac{1}{z^{m-3}}+\text{etc.}$
$\pm$

items.quote:
Hinc igitur primo ſummam huius ſeriei
$\frac{1}{1(a+1)^n}+\frac{1}{2^m(a+2)^n}+\frac{1}{3^m(a+3)^n}+\frac{1}{4^m(a+4)^n}+\text{etc.}=s$
definire licet
items.english: Hence, first, the sum $s$ of this series $\frac{1}{1(a+1)^n}+\frac{1}{2^m(a+2)^n}+\dots$ can be determined.
